title: Sampling Bias in Entrepreneurial Experiments
eligible_reason: Tables 3 and 4, column (1) regress monthly web traffic on post_event (binary, switches on after each product's Product Hunt launch month, 25 monthly launch cohorts Oct 2016 - Oct 2018) with product FE and calendar year-by-month FE, no controls, linear, clustered by product (reghdfe ... absorb(post_id year#month)). The design is a staggered event study in which not-yet-launched products serve as comparisons. The other columns interact post_event with the product's gender focus and are excluded.
design_notes: Product-month panel (sample_regression_panel.dta: 206,875 rows, 174 vars) of products launched on Product Hunt, web visits from SimilarWeb, window -6..+12 months around launch, launch month dropped. Estimation sample: 5,742 products, 101,803 product-months. The paper's identification of sampling bias uses post x femaleness interactions (Tables 3-4 cols 2-5), event studies by gender-focus group (Figures 3-6), and a triple difference with daily newsletter shocks (Tables 6-7). Tables 3 and 4 have Panels A (continuous score) and B (top/bottom quartile indicators) whose column (1) is the same no-interaction regression.
main_or_robustness: main (launch effect is the baseline column; headline estimand is the interaction)
n_adoption_cohorts_note: first post-launch month ranges Nov 2016 - Nov 2018 (computed from the shipped data after the Table 3 sample filters)

specs.treatment_definition: post_event = 1 for months after the product's Product Hunt launch (event_mo >= 1); launch month (event_mo == 0) dropped from the estimation sample; product-specific launch months Oct 2016 - Oct 2018 (25 monthly cohorts, first treated month Nov 2016 - Nov 2018)
specs.time_var: calendar month: year#month (build ym = year*12 + month)
specs.sample_condition: use data/sample_regression_panel.dta; drop if femaleness_text_all4 == .; keep if event_mo in [-6, 12] & event_mo != 0; keep if suggested_count >= 1 & suggested_count <= 11 & ilink_created_at < newsletter_earliest & is_in_newsletter == 0; keep post_id in data/in_sample_ids.dta (merge m:1, keep _m == 3); l_visits non-missing. Reproduced: 103,356 rows, 5,742 products before dropping 1,553 missing l_visits -> 101,803 obs (matches table output).
specs.outcome: l_visits: log(page visits + 1), SimilarWeb monthly web traffic
specs.reported_location: Table 3, Panels A and B, column (1) (identical regression in both panels; tables/table3a.txt and table3b.txt)
specs.notes: Columns 2-5 of each panel add post_event x femaleness score / quartile indicators, post_event x maker_somefemale, or restrict to male makers with interactions: subgroup-by-treatment interactions, excluded. All products are eventually treated (no never-treated); comparisons are not-yet-launched products. Each product is observed only in its own -6..+12 month window, so the panel is unbalanced in calendar time (composition-fixed CSA cells apply); the last cohort has no not-yet-treated comparison. Coefficient is the launch effect, not the paper's headline gender-gap estimand.

specs.notes: visitsnotzero generated at line 724 (and 645 for Table 3) after the sample filters. Same design caveats as Table 3 column (1).

specs.exclusion_reason: post_event x femaleness (continuous or quartile) and post_event x maker_somefemale interactions: subgroup-by-treatment interactions / continuous interaction
event-time x female-focused-group interactions (ib5.time##i.textf_pct75/25), subgroup-by-treatment event study
continuous newsletter-shock interactions (post x shock x score) and extra suggested_count FE
cross-sectional funding / survival regressions with controls

data_provenance_note: README: processed data with anonymized product identifiers (licenses for Product Hunt, BuiltWith, SimilarWeb, Crunchbase, Preqin data prevent disclosing firm identifiers); values appear to be the original data (sample size reproduces the published N exactly). Not described as synthetic or perturbed.
software_notes: Single do-file run_tables_and_figures.do (reghdfe, xtreg, outreg2). Figure 2 data not shipped (proprietary viewing data).
screener_notes: Eligible only through the baseline launch-effect columns; no never-treated units, so CSA/BJS rely on not-yet-treated products and the last launch cohort is unidentified. Each product appears only within its own 19-month event window (unbalanced in calendar time). Table numbering and main-text status inferred from the do-file and outreg file names (no article text). Screened from package only.
